title: How to build savings for major life events (weddings, relocations, etc.)
description: Using time-bucketing to separate your goals from your emergency fund.
content:
Life is full of 'expected surprises.' You know you will eventually need a new car. You know you want to get married or buy a house. Yet, when the bill arrives, it often feels like an emergency because the money wasn't specifically set aside. This leads to raiding the retirement fund or using credit cards. The solution is **Time-Bucketing**. By assigning specific savings accounts to specific timelines and goals, you protect your long-term wealth from short-term life events.

Key Takeaways

  • Segregation of Funds: Do not keep your 'Wedding Fund' in the same account as your 'Job Loss Fund.' Psychologically, you will feel richer than you are and overspend.
  • Asset Matching: Match the investment vehicle to the deadline. <2 years = Cash. 2-5 years = Bonds/CDs. >5 years = Stocks.
  • Sinking Funds: Break a $30,000 goal into monthly payments. Saving $1,000/month is a bill, not a choice.
  • Windfall Allocation: Decide in advance where bonuses go. '50% to House Fund, 50% to Invest.' Remove the decision at the moment of receipt.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The average US wedding costs $30,000. The average down payment is $30,000-$60,000. These are massive capital outlays. High-Yield Savings Accounts (HYSAs) allow you to create 'Vaults' or 'Buckets' to organize these goals visually.

The Bucket Framework

Separate your money by time horizon.

Bucket 1: The Imminent (0-12 Months)

  • Goals: Vacation, Christmas, Moving Costs.
  • Vehicle: HYSA (Ally/Marcus).
  • Risk: Zero. You need liquidity.

Bucket 2: The Intermediate (1-3 Years)

  • Goals: Wedding, Car Purchase, House Down Payment.
  • Vehicle: Treasury Bills, CD Ladder, or Money Market Fund.
  • Risk: Low. Focus on yield optimization (getting 5% vs 0%).

Bucket 3: The Horizon (3-7 Years)

  • Goals: Sabbatical, Dream Home Upgrade.
  • Vehicle: Conservative Portfolio (20% Stocks / 80% Bonds).
  • Risk: Low-Medium. You need to beat inflation, but can't afford a crash. As the date gets closer, move this money to Bucket 1.

Execution Tactics

  1. Name the Account: Log into your bank. Change the nickname of your savings account to 'Wedding 2026'. This visual anchor stops you from raiding it for a weekend trip.
  2. Automate the Divide: Split your direct deposit. $200 to Wedding, $300 to House, $500 to Emergency. Don't let it touch checking.
  3. The 'Gap' Analysis: If you need $20k in 10 months ($2k/mo) but can only save $500/mo, you must either move the date or lower the budget. The math forces a reality check now, not later.
  4. Credit Card Float: Pay for the wedding expenses on a points card, but pay it off weekly from the dedicated savings bucket. Earn the points, avoid the debt.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I invest my house fund?

If buying in <3 years, No. If the market drops 20%, your down payment evaporates, and you can't buy the house. The risk of delay is too high.

Can I use I-Bonds?

Yes, for the 1-5 year bucket. Just remember the 1-year lockup period. You literally cannot access the money.

What if I have an emergency?

Raid the 'Luxury' buckets first. Drain the Vacation fund before you drain the Car Repair fund. Prioritize survival over fun.
